task_description: Build a polished, genuinely playable 3D browser racing game prototype (Phase 1). Stack: Three.js (rendering) + Cannon-es raycast vehicle (arcade-leaning physics), vanilla JS ES modules with a NO-BUILD importmap/CDN setup (mandated by the INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox where npm install and CDNs are unreachable in-sandbox but available to the end user). Deliver: lit/shadowed 3D scene with skybox, drivable car with suspension/grip/accel/drift, keyboard controls (WASD/arrows + handbrake + reset), a designed circuit with barriers and checkpoints, HUD (speedometer, lap timer, lap counter, best-lap), and a game loop with countdown start, checkpoint-based lap detection, and finish. Architecture uses a system-registry seam so later phases (opponent AI, sound, minimap, multiple cars, upgrades) layer in cleanly. Includes README with run instructions and controls.

verification.summary: No-build project: `node scripts/check.mjs` syntax-checks all 22 modules and validates index.html (importmap three+cannon-es, mount, #hud) -> exit 0. `node --test` runs 43 unit tests, all pass, covering pure logic: cameraMath, format, loop, handling (steer/kmh), lap (in-order lap completion, out-of-order/shortcut rejection, crossedGate segment/plane geometry, best-lap), drift (lateralSlip/isDrifting/driftIntensity), systems registry, and mid-race respawn pose. Test quality verified by reading drift.js + lap.js + respawn.test.js: tests exercise real code paths and would fail if the implementation were reverted (not static assertions). Static server verified: GET / -> 200, GET /src/main.js -> 200 with application/javascript, HTML contains the cannon-es importmap entry. No em dashes anywhere in the tree. Docker: no Dockerfile and INTEGRATIONS_ONLY blocks image pulls, so docker build is skipped by design. Full 3D render cannot be verified headless in-sandbox (no browser + CDN unreachable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY); libraries resolve via the importmap in the end user's browser, which is the documented and intended runtime.

verification.semantic_review: APPROVED after fixes (see 2026-09-21-093250-review-visual-audio-overhaul.md); initial verdict was NEEDS_CHANGES with 5 non-blocking issues, all 5 addressed in the post-review fix commits
verification.summary: Full visual/audio overhaul: sculpted procedural car model, asphalt track texture + curbs + centerline, roadside scenery, sunset lighting + rim light + PMREM env map + optional bloom postprocessing (best-effort, degrades gracefully), collision sparks + camera screen-shake, launch/wheelspin dust puff, redesigned dial-speedometer HUD with drift callout/speed lines/finish lap list, and a synthesized Web Audio engine/tire-screech AudioSystem gated on a user gesture. All new deterministic math (dial, shake, audioMath incl. engineBrightness, scenery, speedfx, dust) lives in unit-tested src/game/logic/ pure modules. `node scripts/check.mjs` -> 30 modules OK. `node --test` -> 99/99 pass. No em dashes. Full 3D/audio rendering still cannot be verified headless in this sandbox (no browser, CDN unreachable); this is documented in the README exactly as the Phase 1 task documented it.

known_limitations: The car model, track texture, lighting/bloom/env-map, screen-shake feel, and synthesized audio were not visually/aurally verified in this sandbox (no browser, no audio device, CDN unreachable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY); confidence is architectural and via code review, not observation. A manual browser smoke test is recommended.
The AudioSystem's autoplay-gesture handling and engine/tire-screech synthesis graph were reviewed by reading the code but not exercised (no Web Audio API in this sandbox).
